He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. ==Early life== Reaves was born and grew up in [[Fairfax, Virginia]]. He and his older brother were raised in a single parent household by his Bolivian-born{{Cite web|url=https://www.la-razon.com/marcas/2020/08/31/liset-bravo-el-motor-de-reaves-en-la-nba/|title=Liset Bravo, el 'motor' de Reaves en la NBA}} mother, Liset Bravo Reaves, after his father died when he was six years old. He initially attended Middleburg Academy with [[Mo Alie-Cox]], later transferring to [[Paul VI Catholic High School]], where he played both basketball and soccer.{{cite web|url=https://gopsusports.com/news/2019/2/27/mens-basketball-josh-reaves-a-story-of-perseverance.aspx|title=Josh Reaves: A Story of Perseverance|first=Andy|last=Kuros|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=February 27, 2019}} As a junior, Reaves was named team captain and averaged 12.6 points per game and was named All-Washington Metro Area as the Panthers won the [[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]], VISAA Division I State championship, and the Alhambra Catholic Invitational. Reaves transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] before his senior year.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2014/06/05/joshua-reaves-transfers-from-paul-vi-to-oak-hill-basketball/?noredirect=on|title=Joshua Reaves transfers from Paul VI to Oak Hill basketball|first=Brandon|last=Parker|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=June 5, 2014|access-date=July 30, 2019}} Ranked the 74th-best recruit in the nation and second in state by ''[[ESPN.com]]'', Reaves committed to play college basketball at [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] over offers from [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pennlive.com/sports/2014/07/josh_reaves_commit_signals_pen.html|title=Josh Reaves commit signals Penn State move into talent-rich DC area|first=David|last=Jones|website=[[PennLive.com]]|date=July 3, 2014|access-date=July 30, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.btpowerhouse.com/2015/8/19/9172077/creating-the-hype-for-penn-states-josh-reaves|title=Creating the Hype for Penn State's Josh Reaves|first=Jerry|last=Schwerin|website=BTPowerHouse.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 19, 2015|access-date=July 30, 2019}} He was named Oak Hill's captain as the team went 47–1 and was ranked seventh nationally by [[MaxPreps]] in his only season.{{cite web|url=https://www.collegian.psu.edu/sports/men_basketball/article_60631910-1ce4-11e8-a4b0-e3a9e06365f3.html|title=FEATURE: How Josh Reaves became Penn State men's basketball's catalyst for success|first=Vincent|last=Lungaro|work=[[The Daily Collegian]]|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=July 30, 2019}} ==College career== Reaves played four seasons as a member of the [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. He started 20 games as a freshman and appeared in six more off the bench, despite missing time due to a bout with [[Mononucleosis]], averaging 6.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.blackshoediaries.com/mens-basketball/2016/10/29/13453526/2016-17-penn-state-basketball-player-preview-josh-reaves|title=2016–17 Penn State Basketball Player Preview: Josh Reaves|first=Aaron|last=Yorke|website=BlackShoeDiaries.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=July 30, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.centredaily.com/sports/college/penn-state-university/psu-basketball/article121568342.html|title=Penn State's Josh Reaves finding rhythm since return from early-season injury|first=Ryne|last=Gery|work=[[Centre Daily Times]]|date=December 17, 2016|access-date=July 30, 2019}} As a sophomore, Reaves averaged 7.7 points and four rebounds per game while leading the [[Big Ten]] with 2.14 steals per game (16th-best in the nation).{{cite web|url=https://www.blackshoediaries.com/2017/4/13/14977654/penn-state-basketball-postseason-grades-josh-reaves-pat-chambers-big-ten|title=Penn State Basketball Postseason Grades: Josh Reaves|first=Chris|last=Taylor|website=BlackShoeDiaries.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=April 13, 2017|access-date=July 30, 2019}} In his junior season, Reaves averaged 10.6 points, 5.1 reboundsand 3.2 assists per game and again led the Big Ten with 2.18 steals per game and was named to the Big Ten All-Defensive Team.{{cite web|url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/basketball/men/tom-oates-breaking-down-the---big-ten-men/collection_881ccadc-dc9a-5df3-a308-48c2b614a30f.html|title=Tom Oates: Breaking down the 2018–19 Big Ten men's basketball season|first=Tom|last=Oates|website=[[Madison.com]]|date=November 10, 2018|access-date=July 30, 2019}} He was named the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year, All-Defensive Team, and honorable mention all-conference as a senior after averaging 10.6 points, five rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 blocks per game and leading the Big Ten for the third straight season with 2.5 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.tribdem.com/sports/big-ten-basketball-coaches-honor-penn-state-s-stevens-reaves/article_13873568-446b-11e9-97ce-876793a29f9a.html|title=Big Ten basketball coaches honor Penn State's Stevens, Reaves|work=[[The Tribune-Democrat]]|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=July 30, 2019}} Reaves finished his collegiate career with 1,079 career points, 540 rebounds, 310 assists and 92 shots blocked and set the school record with 250 steals.{{cite web|url=http://www.statecollege.com/news/local-news/penn-state-basketball-josh-reaves-signs-twoway-deal-with-dallas-mavericks,1480688/|title=Penn State Basketball: Josh Reaves Signs Two-Way Deal With Dallas Mavericks|first=Ben|last=Jones|website=StateCollege.com|date=July 30, 2019|access-date=July 31, 2019|archive-date=July 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190731005124/http://www.statecollege.com/news/local-news/penn-state-basketball-josh-reaves-signs-twoway-deal-with-dallas-mavericks,1480688/|url-status=dead}} Following the end of his senior season, Reaves was invited to play in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], where he was named to the All-Tournament team.{{cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/2019/06/10/penn-state-basketball-nba-draft-josh-reaves-interview/|title=2019 NBA draft prospect Josh Reaves: 'Teams love the intensity and passion that I play with'|first=Bryan|last=Kalbrosky|work=[[USA Today]]|date=June 10, 2019|accessdate=August 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== === Dallas Mavericks (2019–2020) === After going unselected in the [[2019 NBA Draft|2019 NBA draft]], Reaves was named to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] roster and averaged 12.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.2 steals and one block per game over five games.{{cite web|url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-mavericks/mavericks/2019/07/29/mavs-sign-penn-states-josh-reaves-two-way-contract|title=Mavs sign Penn State's Josh Reaves to two-way contract|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=July 29, 2019|access-date=July 30, 2019}} Reaves signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Mavericks on July 29, 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-josh-reaves-to-two-way-contract/|title=Mavericks sign Josh Reaves to two-way contract|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 29, 2019|access-date=July 30, 2019}} Reaves made his NBA debut on January 2, 2020, playing the final minute of the 123–111 win against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://onwardstate.com/2020/01/03/josh-reaves-makes-nba-debut-in-dallas-mavericks-123-111-victory-over-brooklyn-nets/|title=Josh Reaves Makes NBA Debut in Dallas Mavericks' 123–111 Victory Over Brooklyn Nets|first=Mikey|last=Mandarino|website=[[Onward State]]|date=January 3, 2020|access-date=January 3, 2020}} On August 10, in a 122–114 victory against the [[Utah Jazz]], Reaves made his first career field goal scoring a layup on a backdoor cut,{{Cite twitter |title=Josh Reaves is on the board with the first points of his NBA career. |number=1292923968337436679 |user=bobbykaralla |first=Bobby |last=Karalla |date=August 10, 2020 |access-date=August 10, 2020 |language=en}}{{Primary source inline|date=August 2020}} and also had his first career rebound and assist; he finished the game with 4 points on 2 of 4 shooting from the field, 1 rebound, and 3 assists in 14 minutes of playing time.{{Cite web|title=Mavericks vs. Jazz – Box Score – August 10, 2020 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401224768|access-date=August 10, 2020|publisher=ESPN|language=en}} === Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2021) === On December 19, 2020, Reaves signed with the [[Houston Rockets]], but was waived on the same day{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Rockets Sign, Waive Josh Reaves|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/rockets-sign-waive-josh-reaves.html|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 19, 2020|accessdate=April 13, 2021}} and on January 18, 2021, he signed with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title=Vipers Finalize 2021 Roster|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-finalize-2021-roster/|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2021|accessdate=April 13, 2021}} Reaves played in each of the Vipers' 15 games in the COVID-shortened 2020–21 season, averaging 12 points, 2.7 assists, and 4.4 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |title=Josh Reaves G-League Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/r/reavejo01d.html |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} Reaves scored 7 points in 28 minutes in the Vipers' 110-81 G League Quarterfinal loss to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Warriors 110-81 Vipers (Mar 8, 2021) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba-g-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401310613 |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=ESPN |language=en}} === Beşiktaş (2021–2022) === On July 5, 2021, Reaves signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) in Turkey.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/josh-reaves-joins-besiktas/|title=Josh Reaves joins Besiktas|last=|first=|date=July 5, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 5, 2021}} Reaves played in 23 games for Beşiktaş, averaging 5.0 points, 1.3 assists, and 2.1 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |title=Josh Reaves International Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/josh-reaves-1.html |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} Beşiktaş went 15-15 and failed to qualify for the BSL playoffs.{{Cite web |title=Türkiye Sigorta Basketbol Süper Ligi - 2021-22 Standings and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/turkey-super-league/2022.html |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} === Tofaş (2022) === On September 13, 2022, Reaves signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=http://tofasspor.com/haber-2591-josh_reaves_tofasta|title=Josh Reaves Tofaş'ta|last=|first=|date=September 13, 2022|website=tofasspor.com|publisher=|language=tr|access-date=September 15, 2022}} On October 26, Tofaş announced that it had parted ways with Reaves by mutual agreement.{{Cite web |title=TOFAŞ’TA JOSH REAVES İLE YOLLAR AYRILDI |url=http://www.24saniye.com/Haber/58171 |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=www.24saniye.com}} Reaves did not appear in any league games for Tofaş.{{Cite web |title=2022-23 Stats - Tofaş |url=https://www.basketball-reference.cominternational/teams/tofas/2023.html |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Return to Rio Grande (2022–2025)=== On November 3, 2022, Reaves was named to the opening night roster for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title=Vipers Finalize 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-finalize-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895553|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} Reaves played in 14 games for the Vipers in the 2022–23 regular season, averaging 7.4 points, 2.7 assists, and 2.9 rebounds per game. He played in all five of the team's playoff games, including a total of 9 points in the G-League Finals, which the Vipers lost in two games to the Delaware Blue Coats.{{Cite web |title=DEL vs RGV |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2042200402/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=NBA G League Stats |language=en}} ==Bolivia national team== Reaves plays for the [[Bolivia men's national basketball team|Bolivian national team]] where he has been the key player.{{cite news|title=Básquetbol: Bolivia hace prevalecer su localía ante Ecuador|url=https://jornada.com.bo/basquetbol-bolivia-hace-prevalecer-su-localia-ante-ecuador/ |accessdate=23 July 2021 |work=[[Jornada (La Paz)|Jornada]] |date=12 June 2021 |language=Spanish}} At the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)]], he led Bolivia in points, assists, steals and blocks.[http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/americas-pre-qualifiers/team/Bolivia Bolivia FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 Americas Pre-Qualifiers 2021] [[FIBA]], 15 July 2021.
